problem_statement.title: Functions in channel_props can be shadowed by their submodules ("'module' object is not callable")
problem_statement.body:
## Before reporting this bug:
- [x] Verify there is not an existing issue for it already
- [x] You are using the latest version of `toqito` with a Python version `>=3.12`

## Describe the bug
`toqito.channel_props` loads its functions lazily through a module-level `__getattr__`. Each function lives in a submodule with the same name (`channel_props/channel_dim.py` defines `channel_dim`, and so on).

When any code imports one of those submodules directly, for example `from toqito.channel_props.channel_dim import channel_dim` (which `choi_to_kraus`, `kraus_to_choi`, `dual_channel`, `channel_distinguishability` and others do), Python sets the submodule as an attribute of the package. After that, `__getattr__` is never called for that name, so `from toqito.channel_props import channel_dim` gives the module instead of the function.

Whether it breaks depends on import order. After importing every module in `toqito`, 8 of the 12 names in `channel_props.__all__` resolve to modules: `channel_dim`, `choi_rank`, `is_channel_antidistinguishable`, `is_extremal`, `is_positive`, `is_unital`, `is_unitary`, `is_unitary_antidistinguishable`.

## To Reproduce
```python
from toqito.channel_ops import choi_to_kraus  # imports toqito.channel_props.channel_dim
from toqito.channel_props import channel_dim

print(type(channel_dim))  # <class 'module'>
channel_dim([[1, 0], [0, 1]])  # TypeError: 'module' object is not callable
```

Without the first line, `channel_dim` is the function as expected.

## Expected behavior
`from toqito.channel_props import <name>` should always give the function, whatever was imported before.

Going back to eager imports in `__init__.py` is not an option, because that reintroduces circular imports (`matrix_props.sk_norm`, `channel_opt.channel_distinguishability`). A small fix that keeps the lazy loading is to give the package module a `__setattr__` that, when Python sets one of the `__all__` submodules on the package, stores the function from that submodule instead.

## System Information where `toqito` is installed
toqito master (c3fdb0f), Python 3.13

I have a fix with a regression test ready and will open a PR. (I used Claude to help find and fix this.)

problem_statement.title: Oracle: TO_DATE and TO_TIMESTAMP silently drop the nlsparam argument
problem_statement.body:
With `read="oracle"`, the third argument (`nlsparam`) of `TO_DATE` and `TO_TIMESTAMP` is silently dropped:

```
input:  TO_DATE(c, 'DD-MON-YYYY', 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE = American')
output: TO_DATE(c, 'DD-MON-YYYY')
```

Oracle accepts up to three arguments (`char`, `fmt`, `nlsparam`), but sqlglot only keeps the first two, with no error or warning.

**Before you file an issue**
- Read dialect: `oracle`
- Write dialect: `oracle`
- Checked on main (6de2df31b), also reproduced on 30.18.0

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

The first two queries are the examples from the Oracle docs for `TO_DATE` and `TO_TIMESTAMP`.

```python
import sqlglot

for sql in [
    "SELECT TO_DATE('January 15, 1989, 11:00 A.M.', 'Month dd, YYYY, HH:MI A.M.', 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE = American') FROM DUAL",
    "SELECT TO_TIMESTAMP('10-Sep-02 14:10:10.123000', 'DD-Mon-RR HH24:MI:SS.FF', 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE = American') FROM DUAL",
    "SELECT TO_DATE(:p1, 'DD-MON-YYYY', :p2) FROM DUAL",
]:
    print(sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="oracle").sql(dialect="oracle"))
```

Actual output:

```
SELECT TO_DATE('January 15, 1989, 11:00 A.M.', 'Month dd, YYYY, HH12:MI A.M.') FROM DUAL
SELECT TO_TIMESTAMP('10-Sep-02 14:10:10.123000', 'DD-Mon-RR HH24:MI:SS.FF') FROM DUAL
SELECT TO_DATE(:p1, 'DD-MON-YYYY') FROM DUAL
```

In all three cases the third argument is gone. Expected: it is kept, e.g. `TO_DATE('January 15, 1989, 11:00 A.M.', 'Month dd, YYYY, HH12:MI A.M.', 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE = American')`.

Dropping it changes what the query does. `nlsparam` sets the language used to read month and day names like `January` or `Sep`. Without it, Oracle falls back to the session's `NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE`, so the generated SQL can fail or behave differently on a session whose language isn't English.

**Official Documentation**

Both functions document the same signature:

```
TO_DATE(char [ DEFAULT return_value ON CONVERSION ERROR ] [, fmt [, 'nlsparam' ] ])
TO_TIMESTAMP(char [ DEFAULT return_value ON CONVERSION ERROR ] [, fmt [, 'nlsparam' ] ])
```

From the TO_DATE page: "The 'nlsparam' argument specifies the language of the text string that is being converted to a date." The TO_TIMESTAMP page says it "has the same purpose in this function as in the TO_CHAR function for date conversion."

- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/TO_DATE.html
- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/TO_TIMESTAMP.html

I have a fix ready and will open a PR shortly (prepared with help from Claude).

title: Release (tag at ship): a session file whose body names another conversation never overwrites it (#8859) (#8859)
issue_title: A copied sidecar whose body names another session overwrites that session's conversation on its first load

install_config.install: pip install -q pyyaml && pip install -q pytest pytest-timeout

gold_patch:
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 3a6692b4c5b..8e16cebafe3 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -101,6 +101,8 @@
 
 ### Fixed
 
+- **A session file whose body names a different conversation no longer overwrites that conversation.** A sidecar copied by hand or restored from a backup under another name was loaded with the id its body names, so the load's duplicate-partial cleanup, any later save, a chat started on it, a background wakeup, the stale-stream repair, a workspace rebind or a reasoning-effort change wrote the original conversation instead, replacing its transcript and moving it to another profile; a body with no id left a stray file on every load. Such a file is now marked on load and never written: every save path refuses it, a chat or wakeup started on its id answers 404 before anything changes, and the stale-state repairs keep their fixes in memory only. Loading, the session list and the self-heal for files the server wrote are unchanged. (#8859, #8852)
+
 - **Two test files no longer fail when another file runs first.** Stubbed-agent tests in `tests/test_security_redaction.py` reloaded `api.helpers` under a stub and "restored" it under the same stub, so a later redaction test saw the stub redactor (#8845); a test in `tests/test_chat_start_orphan_stream_recovery.py` could leave a stream registered, which flipped two idle CLI-cache tests in `tests/test_claude_code_session_import.py` (#8850). The stub tests now swap in a stub redactor without reloading the module, the stream-recovery tests reset their registries after each test as well as before, the two cache tests pin the idle mode they assert, and the large-string redaction fixture names the cause when the module is not bound to the live Agent redactor. Test-only; no production code changes. (#8866, #8845, #8850)
 
 - **Samsung photos no longer stall a session or come back corrupted (#8805).** Photos from Samsung phones carry a Samsung Extended Format (SEF) trailer after the JPEG data, so they failed the check that lets a complete image skip credential redaction. Every load of a session holding them ran the redaction patterns over megabytes of base64: a 52 MB session took 67-79 s per load, and the redaction pass also altered the photo in the response so it no longer decoded (the saved session was untouched). A trailer that is exactly one well-formed SEF block set, fully accounted for with nothing after it, is now accepted; a malformed or partial trailer is still redacted. Thanks @jan-demsar. (#8809)

                 f"Refusing to save session {self.session_id!r}: messages must be a list, "
@@ -2494,10 +2505,26 @@ def load(cls, sid):
         # vouched for.

+        elif _collapsed_partials:
             try:
                 # Self-heal bloated sessions on first full load without touching
                 # recency/index ordering; save() creates a .bak because this

+"""#8852: a sidecar whose body names another session never writes that session.
+
+``Session.load(sid)`` builds the session from the file's body, so ``session.session_id`` is
+whatever the body says, and ``save()`` writes ``SESSION_DIR / f"{session_id}.json"``. A sidecar
+whose body names a different session (a manual copy, or a backup restored under another name)
+therefore overwrote that other session:
+
+- on its first load, through the duplicate-partial collapse save (no request needed: an index
+  rebuild loads every file);
+- on any later save of the loaded object, whatever triggered it.
+
+A sidecar with no ``session_id`` at all got a random id, and each collapse load wrote a new
+stray file under it.
+
+``Session.load`` (and the metadata-only loader) now marks a session whose body doesn't name the
+file it was read from, keeps the collapse in memory only, and ``save()`` refuses to write a marked
+session; so does the one writer that patches a sidecar without ``save()`` (workspace recovery).
+``POST /api/chat/start`` answers a marked session 404 before mutating anything. What a load returns and
+what the session list shows are unchanged. The server never writes such a file itself: every
+sidecar it saves carries its own id.
+"""
+
+import io
+import json
+import logging
+import urllib.parse
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from pathlib import Path

+import pytest

+VICTIM = "victim-8852"
+COPY = "copy-8852"

+    monkeypatch.setattr(routes, "_get_active_profile_name", lambda: "default")

+def _copy(directory, *, partials=True, body_id=VICTIM, name=COPY):
+    """A sidecar named `name` whose body names `body_id` (None: no session_id key at all)."""
+    raw = json.loads((directory / f"{VICTIM}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

+    import api.routes as routes
+    from api import models
+
+    _mid_turn_copy(store)
+    before = _files(store)
+    with config.STREAMS_LOCK:
+        config.STREAMS["dead-stream"] = object()
+    try:
+        session = models.get_session(COPY)
+        assert routes._clear_stale_stream_state(session) is False
+        state = (session.pending_user_message, session.active_stream_id)
+    finally:
+        with config.STREAMS_LOCK:
+            config.STREAMS.pop("dead-stream", None)
+
+    assert state == ("half-sent", "dead-stream")
+    assert _files(store) == before
+
+
+def test_the_reasoning_writer_refuses_a_session_loaded_from_a_copy(store):
+    """``set_session_reasoning_effort`` given a session object patches that object's sidecar
+    directly, without ``save()``. Over HTTP the generic ownership guard 404s the copy first
+    (``/api/reasoning``); this covers a direct caller."""
+    from api import models
+
+    _victim(store)
+    _copy(store, partials=False)
+    before = _files(store)
+
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="8852"):
+        models.set_session_reasoning_effort(models.get_session(COPY), "high")
+
+    _unchanged_victim(store, before)
+    assert _files(store) == before
+
+
+def test_the_title_writer_refuses_a_session_loaded_from_a_copy(store):
+    """``_persist_generated_session_title`` reloads the session the object's id names and saves
+    it, so a copy object would retitle the session its body names. Over HTTP the generic
+    ownership guard 404s the copy first (``/api/session/title/regenerate``), and the import
+    title thread loads the imported session by its own id; this covers a direct caller."""
+    from api import models, routes
+
+    _victim(store)
+    _copy(store, partials=False)
+    before = _files(store)
+
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="8852"):
+        routes._persist_generated_session_title(
+            models.get_session(COPY), "Hijacked by copy", event_reason="test"
+        )
+
+    _unchanged_victim(store, before)
+    assert _files(store) == before
+    assert json.loads(before[f"{VICTIM}.json"])["title"] == "Victim"
+
+
+def test_gateway_reattach_at_startup_skips_a_copy(store, monkeypatch):
+    """At startup every sidecar with an active stream and a saved Gateway run is reattached under
+    its session's id. A copy's id is the other session's, so its stale run would be resumed, and
+    its answer written back, there."""
+    import api.config as config
+    import api.gateway_chat as gateway_chat
+
+    launched = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gateway_chat, "_run_gateway_chat_streaming", lambda *a, **k: launched.append((a, k)))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gateway_chat, "_gateway_endpoint_for_profile", lambda profile: "http://127.0.0.1:9")
+    _mid_turn_copy(store, gateway=True)
+    before = _files(store)
+    try:
+        resumed = gateway_chat.resume_gateway_runs_after_restart()
+        with config.STREAMS_LOCK:
+            registered = "dead-stream" in config.STREAMS
+    finally:
+        with config.STREAMS_LOCK:
+            config.STREAMS.pop("dead-stream", None)
+        config.CANCEL_FLAGS.pop("dead-stream", None)

+    assert (resumed, registered, launched) == ([], False, [])
+    _unchanged_victim(store, before)
+    assert _files(store) == before
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("partials", [True, False])
+def test_a_background_wakeup_for_a_copy_is_dropped_cleanly(store, monkeypatch, caplog, partials):
+    """``start_session_turn`` (process and delegation wakeups) is the server-side twin of chat/start.
+    On a copy it raised from the save guard, which its contract says never happens, and left the
+    cached copy mid-turn; the process-wakeup runner re-queued the wakeup and logged a traceback on
+    every drain (senior review, round 3). It now answers the 404 its callers drop, before anything
+    is mutated, and the owner's own wakeup still starts."""

problem_statement.title: A copied sidecar whose body names another session overwrites that session's conversation on its first load
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

`Session.load(sid)` collapses adjacent duplicate `_partial` rows and then calls `session.save(touch_updated_at=False, skip_index=True)` (`api/models.py`, `Session.load`, the `if _collapsed_partials:` branch). `save()` writes `SESSION_DIR / f"{self.session_id}.json"`, and `self.session_id` comes from the file's **body**, not from the `sid` that was loaded.

So a sidecar whose body names a different session (for example `copy.json` containing `"session_id": "victim"`) and has duplicate partials **overwrites `victim.json` with its own transcript and profile** the first time anything loads it. `copy.json` itself is left unchanged.

No request is needed. Listing sessions with the index missing rebuilds it, and the rebuild loads the copy.

## Reproduced (v0.52.544 and exp-v0.52.638)

The setup is a `victim-8834.json` with 5 turns and profile `work`, plus a `copy-8834.json` whose body says `"session_id": "victim-8834"`, profile `default`, holding `[user, partial, partial]`.

| trigger | victim before | victim after | `victim.json.bak` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Session.load("copy-8834")` | 5 rows, `work` | 2 rows, `default` | 5 rows |
| `all_sessions()` with no `_index.json` (no request) | 5 rows | 2 rows | 5 rows |
| 3 repeated loads of the copy | 5 rows | 2 rows each time | still 5 rows |

The original transcript survives only in the single `.bak` generation. A later shrinking save of `victim` replaces it.

## Fix shape

Persist the collapse only when the body names the file being loaded:
- if `session.session_id != sid`, keep the in-memory collapse, skip the save, and log it;
- if the body has no `session_id` at all, `Session(**data)` generates a random id, so skip the save in that case too.

This is the same rule #8833 applied to its share-field repair: a repair writes the record that was asked for, never an id read from the record's own body.

## Scope and related

- **Trigger:** a sidecar whose filename stem differs from its body `session_id`, e.g. a manual copy or a backup restored under another name. Sync-conflict copies usually aren't affected: their names contain dots or spaces, which `is_safe_session_id` rejects.
- **#8834:** separate from #8834 (refused requests still run this save). #8834's fix keeps the three refusing routes from loading such a file (unverifiable ownership fails closed, as in #8094), but background loads still reach this save.
- **Write paths:** this is the only write this probe found. Other derived writes keyed by the body id (index rows) were not checked here.

problem_statement.title: Sub-chunk slicing of an uncompressed ManifestArray ignores inlined chunks
problem_statement.body:
### What happened

Slicing an uncompressed `ManifestArray` within a single chunk (the sub-chunk path added in #996) shifts the offset and length of each virtual chunk reference, but leaves inlined chunks untouched. The sliced array keeps the full inlined chunk bytes while its metadata describes the smaller chunk, so reading it fails:

```
ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 10 into shape (3,)
```

Inlined chunks are common for small coordinate variables, for example from kerchunk references or `HDFParser`.

### Minimal example

```python
import numpy as np
import zarr
from obspec_utils.registry import ObjectStoreRegistry

from virtualizarr.manifests import ChunkManifest, ManifestArray, ManifestGroup, ManifestStore
from virtualizarr.manifests.utils import create_v3_array_metadata

data = np.arange(10, dtype="<i4")
metadata = create_v3_array_metadata(shape=(10,), data_type=data.dtype, chunk_shape=(10,))
manifest = ChunkManifest(
    entries={"0": {"path": "", "offset": 0, "length": 40, "data": data.tobytes()}}
)
marr = ManifestArray(metadata=metadata, chunkmanifest=manifest)

sliced = marr[2:5]
print(sliced.shape)  # (3,)
print(len(sliced.manifest.dict()["0"]["data"]))  # 40, expected 12

store = ManifestStore(group=ManifestGroup(arrays={"a": sliced}), registry=ObjectStoreRegistry())
zarr.open_array(store, path="a", mode="r")[:]  # ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 10 into shape (3,)
```

### What you expected to happen

`[2 3 4]`, the same result as for a virtual chunk reference to the same bytes.

### Cause

`_shift_manifest_byte_ranges` in `virtualizarr/manifests/indexing.py` copies the inlined chunks unchanged. Inlined chunks of an uncompressed array hold raw bytes in the same layout, so they need the same `[offset_delta : offset_delta + new_length]` trim.

### Environment

VirtualiZarr `main` (cc44bae), zarr 3.4.2, xarray 2026.9.0, Python 3.12.

problem_statement.title: [Torch backend] keras.ops.moments returns zero variance for nonconstant float32 input
problem_statement.body:
**Issue type**
Bug.
**Keras version**
3.10.0. Backends: TensorFlow 2.16.1 and PyTorch 2.2.0+cpu. NumPy 1.26.4.
**Python version**
3.12.14.
**Current behavior**
On the Torch backend, keras.ops.moments returns variance 0 for the float32 values [10000, 10001, 10002, 10003]. Their population variance is exactly 1.25. Consequently, a training-mode BatchNormalization layer returns [-24, -8, 8, 24] with epsilon=0.00390625, instead of values near [-1.33955, -0.44652, 0.44652, 1.33955].
Expected: a variance close to 1.25 and normalized values close to a centered float64 reference, within appropriate float32 error. Bitwise agreement with TensorFlow is not required; TensorFlow also has small rounding errors in the normalization result.
The [Keras 3.10.0 Torch implementation](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/v3.10.0/keras/src/backend/torch/nn.py#L776) computes variance as mean(x*x) - mean(x)**2. Subtracting these large, nearly equal float32 quantities loses the small variance. The same formula remains in the [source inspected on 2026-10-09](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/4818beec3dd6557b42c596cb316fc835d3b329f8/keras/src/backend/torch/ops/nn.py#L1055). This source inspection is not a runtime reproduction on a current release or Nightly.
Related: [#23751](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/issues/23751) discusses integer dtype rules and a bfloat16 moments example. This reproduction already uses float32 and isolates cancellation caused by the large mean.
This report is counted as an issue under our differential test oracle: on the same saved input, initial weights and execution settings, at least one finite tensor coordinate satisfies both abs(a-b) > 0.15 and its dtype-aware relative-error bound. The original exclusions for nondifferentiable/stateful execution, complex tensors and extreme scale are applied per qualified channel. This oracle classification does not claim maintainer confirmation or identify an unverified root cause.
Could the maintainers confirm whether this float32 cancellation example is the same underlying problem as #23751, or should it be tracked separately from its bfloat16 promotion case?
**Standalone code to reproduce the issue**
Save as repro.py. Run python repro.py tensorflow and python repro.py torch in separate processes.
import os
import sys
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = sys.argv[1]
os.environ["TF_ENABLE_ONEDNN_OPTS"] = "0"
os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "-1"
 
import numpy as np
import keras
 
x = np.array([[10000], [10001], [10002], [10003]], dtype="float32")
mean, variance = keras.ops.moments(x, axes=[0])
bn = keras.layers.BatchNormalization(
    center=False, scale=False, epsilon=0.00390625
)
print(keras.ops.convert_to_numpy(mean))
print(keras.ops.convert_to_numpy(variance))
print(keras.ops.convert_to_numpy(bn(x, training=True)).ravel())
 
reference = x.astype("float64")
reference -= reference.mean(axis=0)
reference /= np.sqrt(np.mean(reference ** 2, axis=0) + 0.00390625)
print(reference.ravel())
**Relevant log output**
Recorded numerical values from the minimal reproduction, with formatting normalized:
TensorFlow:
mean = [10001.5]
variance = [1.25]
BatchNormalization =
[-1.33984375 -0.447265625 0.4462890625 1.3388671875]
 
Torch:
mean = [10001.5]
variance = [0.]
BatchNormalization = [-24. -8. 8. 24.]
 
Centered float64 reference:
[-1.3395493732462742 -0.4465164577487581
  0.4465164577487581  1.3395493732462742]
This mechanism also explains the first significant BatchNormalization differences in saved model cases 000133 and 000188. Their isolated layers reproduced the saved outputs exactly. No additional backward-correctness claim is made: the generated case 000188 had nonfinite input gradients and did not provide a qualified gradient comparison.

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: SBOM shows the resolved version, not the wheel version, when the wheel has a local version
problem_statement.body:
**Related:** #1370, #1371

## Why this is a bug

Fromager can build a wheel that has a local version, for example `0.5.5+local.1`.
A patch can add the local version.
The SBOM in the wheel does not show this version. The SBOM shows the resolved version `0.5.5`.

PR #1371 makes the document name and namespace use the `purl.version` value.
If `purl.version` is not set, the SBOM still uses the resolved version in all fields.

- The SBOM must identify the wheel that contains it. At this time, the SBOM identifies the upstream release.
- The wheel file name and the `METADATA` file show `0.5.5+local.1`. The SBOM shows `0.5.5`. The data in one wheel does not agree.
- Scanners use the SBOM version and purl to find vulnerabilities. A scanner can think that the wheel is the upstream release.
  Then the scanner can show vulnerabilities that a patch fixed. The scanner can also miss the local changes.
- You can set `purl.version` for each package to get the correct version.
  If you forget this setting, fromager does not show an error or a warning. The SBOM is incorrect, and nobody knows.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install fromager from the `main` branch, at commit `45241aad` or a later commit.
   Fromager 0.101.0 also shows the problem.
2. Make the file `overrides/settings.yaml` with this content:

   ```yaml
   sbom:
     supplier: "Organization: ExampleCo"
     namespace: "https://sbom.example"
   ```

3. Make the directory `overrides/patches/sqlparse-0.5.5/`.
4. Put this patch in the directory. Use the name `0001-local-version.patch`.
   The patch changes the package version to `0.5.5+local.1`.

   ```diff
   --- a/sqlparse/__init__.py
   +++ b/sqlparse/__init__.py
   @@ -18,7 +18,7 @@
    from sqlparse import formatter


   -__version__ = "0.5.5"
   +__version__ = "0.5.5+local.1"
    __all__ = ["engine", "filters", "formatter", "sql", "tokens", "cli"]


   ```

5. Do not make a package settings file for `sqlparse`. Do not set `purl.version`.
6. Build the wheel:

   ```bash
   fromager bootstrap sqlparse==0.5.5
   ```

7. Find the wheel in `wheels-repo/downloads/`. Make sure that the file name contains `0.5.5+local.1`.
8. Show the SBOM values:

   ```bash
   WHL=$(ls wheels-repo/downloads/sqlparse-*.whl)
   unzip -p "$WHL" '*.dist-info/sboms/fromager.spdx.json' \
     | jq '.name, .packages[0].versionInfo, .packages[0].externalRefs[0].referenceLocator'
   ```

9. Compare the values with the correct values.

   Actual values:

   ```text
   "sqlparse-0.5.5"
   "0.5.5"
   "pkg:pypi/sqlparse@0.5.5"
   ```

   Correct values:

   ```text
   "sqlparse-0.5.5+local.1"
   "0.5.5+local.1"
   "pkg:pypi/sqlparse@0.5.5%2Blocal.1"
   ```

problem_statement.title: [Regridder] Regridded field shifted by 180° in longitude for lon-lat sources stored on [-180, 180]
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

Since the longitude `range_convention: "0_to_360"` of the `aqua` data model (introduced in
efcb97b09, first released in v1.2.0), `Reader.regrid()` returns a field shifted by 180° in
longitude for any global regular lon-lat source stored on [-180, 180). The coordinates of
the output are correct, the values are not: e.g. MSWEP July precipitation regridded to
r100 puts about 2.6 mm/day over the Sahara (native value 0).

Checked with AQUA 1.2.3 (`main` at 999c9e31c, 2026-10-30) on LUMI. Affected sources found:

- `obs` `MSWEP` `v2.8` `monthly-zarr` and `monthly-netcdf` (stored on [-179.95, 179.95]);
- `obs` `BERKELEY-EARTH` `aqua-filled` `r100-monthly` and `r025-monthly` (stored on [-179.5, 179.5] / [-179.875, 179.875]).

Not affected: ERA5 (stored on [0, 360)) and E-OBS (regional, the wrap is skipped by the
safety check in `normalize_range_convention`).

## Cause

1. `CoordTransformer.normalize_range_convention` wraps the longitudes into [0, 360) and
   `sortby(lon)`, i.e. it rolls the data along `lon` by half the domain.
2. The regridding weights are generated from the grid as stored (via `_retrieve_plain`,
   [-180, 180) order); `_fix_datamodel_weights` applies the data model with
   `flip_coords=False` to the weight coordinates only.
3. Before regridding, `Reader.regrid` calls `counter_reverse_coordinate`, which undoes only
   coordinates carrying the `flipped` attribute (latitude), not the longitude wrap/sort.
4. smmregrid applies the weights by flattened index, so the source cells are read in the
   wrong longitude order.

## Reproduce

Compares `Reader.regrid()` to r100 with a 1° box mean of the native data (the 0.1°/0.25°
cell edges align with the r100 cells, so the box mean is a conservative remap), with and
without the data model.

```python
import warnings

import numpy as np
import aqua
from aqua import Reader

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
print("AQUA", aqua.__version__)

CASES = [
    dict(catalog="obs", model="MSWEP", exp="v2.8", source="monthly-zarr", var="tprate", factor=10),
    dict(catalog="obs", model="BERKELEY-EARTH", exp="aqua-filled", source="r025-monthly", var="2t", factor=4),
    dict(catalog="obs", model="BERKELEY-EARTH", exp="aqua-filled", source="r100-monthly", var="2t", factor=1),
]


def corr(a, b):
    a, b = a.values.ravel(), b.values.ravel()
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    return np.corrcoef(a[ok], b[ok])[0, 1]


def rms(a, b):
    return float(np.sqrt(((a - b) ** 2).mean()))


def check(case, datamodel):
    kwargs = {} if datamodel else {"datamodel": False}
    reader = Reader(catalog=case["catalog"], model=case["model"], exp=case["exp"], source=case["source"],
                    regrid="r100", startdate="2017-07-01", enddate="2017-07-31", loglevel="ERROR", **kwargs)
    native = reader.retrieve(var=case["var"])[case["var"]].isel(time=0)
    regridded = reader.regrid(native).load()
    # without the data model the coordinates keep their stored names
    native = native.rename({c: n for c, n in (("latitude", "lat"), ("longitude", "lon")) if c in native.dims})
    lon_range = f"[{float(native.lon.min()):.2f}, {float(native.lon.max()):.2f}]"
    box = native.sortby("lat").sortby("lon").coarsen(lat=case["factor"], lon=case["factor"]).mean().load()
    box = box.assign_coords(lon=(box.lon % 360)).sortby("lon")
    box = box.assign_coords(lat=regridded.lat, lon=regridded.lon)  # same cells, rounding only
    rolled = box.roll(lon=180, roll_coords=False)
    print(f"{case['model']:15s} {case['source']:13s} datamodel={str(datamodel):5s} lon after retrieve {lon_range:18s} "
          f"regrid vs box mean: corr {corr(regridded, box):.3f} RMS {rms(regridded, box):.3g} | "
          f"vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr {corr(regridded, rolled):.3f} RMS {rms(regridded, rolled):.3g}")


for case in CASES:
    for datamodel in (True, False):
        check(case, datamodel)
```

### Output 

LUMI, AQUA 1.2.3, smmregrid 0.2.0; units: MSWEP kg m-2 s-1, Berkeley Earth K

```
MSWEP           monthly-zarr  datamodel=True  lon after retrieve [0.05, 359.95]     regrid vs box mean: corr 0.257 RMS 4.26e-05 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 0.989 RMS 5.11e-06
MSWEP           monthly-zarr  datamodel=False lon after retrieve [-179.95, 179.95]  regrid vs box mean: corr 0.989 RMS 5.11e-06 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 0.257 RMS 4.26e-05
BERKELEY-EARTH  r025-monthly  datamodel=True  lon after retrieve [0.12, 359.88]     regrid vs box mean: corr 0.925 RMS 8.73 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 1.000 RMS 0.498
BERKELEY-EARTH  r025-monthly  datamodel=False lon after retrieve [-179.88, 179.88]  regrid vs box mean: corr 1.000 RMS 0.498 |vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 0.925 RMS 8.73
BERKELEY-EARTH  r100-monthly  datamodel=True  lon after retrieve [0.50, 359.50]     regrid vs box mean: corr 0.925 RMS 8.72 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 1.000 RMS 0.456
BERKELEY-EARTH  r100-monthly  datamodel=False lon after retrieve [-179.50, 179.50]  regrid vs box mean: corr 1.000 RMS 0.456 |vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 0.925 RMS 8.72
```

With the default data model the regridded field matches the box mean **rolled by 180°**;
with `datamodel=False` it matches the box mean. For temperature the correlation stays high
(0.925) because of the meridional gradient, so the error is easy to miss; the RMS error is
8.7 K.

**Impact**

Any bias/climatology against these references computed with AQUA >= 1.2.0 (e.g. the AQUA
Biases diagnostic with MSWEP or Berkeley Earth as reference) is wrong.

It is not a stale weights/areas problem: with `Reader(..., rebuild=True)` the weights are
regenerated (new files on 2026-11-02 with AQUA 1.2.3) and the result is identical:

```
MSWEP           monthly-zarr  datamodel=True  rebuild=True  regrid vs box mean: corr 0.257 RMS 4.26e-05 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 0.989 RMS 5.11e-06
BERKELEY-EARTH  r100-monthly  datamodel=True  rebuild=True  regrid vs box mean: corr 0.925 RMS 8.72 | vs box mean rolled 180 deg: corr 1.000 RMS 0.456
```

The weights follow the stored grid, which is consistent; the data passed to them are not.

## Workaround

Read the reference with `datamodel=False` (in a diagnostic config:
`reader_kwargs: {datamodel: false}` in the reference entry). The regridded output is on the
target grid in [0, 360) anyway.

## Possible fix

Undo the longitude wrap/sort before `regrid` (as `counter_reverse_coordinate` does for the
latitude flip, e.g. mark the wrapped coordinate and restore the stored order), or build the
weights from the data after the data model has been applied.

problem_statement.title: Partition-scoped position deletes are not applied in NaN identity partitions
problem_statement.body:
### Apache Iceberg version

0.12.0 (latest release)

### Please describe the bug 🐞

Scans can return deleted rows with no error on tables written by Spark or Java. This happens in a NaN identity partition when a position delete file covers more than one data file.

I reproduced the scan failure on 0.12.0 and main at `e3564a54c10960307147377c578680276865ed18`, with Python 3.12 and PyArrow 25.0.1 on Linux/amd64. The same script returns the correct rows on 0.10.0. The bug affects 0.11.0 and later.

The reproduction uses synthetic data in a v2 table identity-partitioned on a `double` column. Each partition, `1.0` and NaN, has two data files. One position delete file per partition deletes position 0 from both data files, without `file_path` bounds. Because PyIceberg cannot write delete files, the script writes the Parquet files with PyArrow and commits them through `fast_append()` and a small delete-manifest writer, in the shape that Spark or Java would produce.

Install `pyiceberg[pyarrow,sql-sqlite]==0.12.0` and `pyarrow==25.0.1`. The script runs unchanged on main and 0.10.0.

```python
import os
import tempfile

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog
from pyiceberg.manifest import DataFile, DataFileContent, FileFormat, ManifestContent, ManifestWriterV2
from pyiceberg.partitioning import PartitionField, PartitionSpec
from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
from pyiceberg.transforms import IdentityTransform
from pyiceberg.typedef import Record
from pyiceberg.types import DoubleType, IntegerType, NestedField

a, b = Record(float("nan")), Record(float("nan"))
print(f"Record(nan) == Record(nan): {a == b}; hashes equal: {hash(a) == hash(b)}")

warehouse = tempfile.mkdtemp()
catalog = SqlCatalog("default", uri=f"sqlite:///{warehouse}/catalog.db", warehouse=f"file://{warehouse}")
catalog.create_namespace("default")
schema = Schema(NestedField(1, "id", IntegerType()), NestedField(2, "value", DoubleType()))
spec = PartitionSpec(PartitionField(source_id=2, field_id=1000, transform=IdentityTransform(), name="value"))
tbl = catalog.create_table("default.t", schema=schema, partition_spec=spec, properties={"format-version": "2"})

pos_delete_schema = pa.schema(
    [
        pa.field("file_path", pa.string(), nullable=False, metadata={"PARQUET:field_id": "2147483546"}),
        pa.field("pos", pa.int64(), nullable=False, metadata={"PARQUET:field_id": "2147483545"}),
    ]
)


def write_file(name: str, rows: pa.Table, value: float, content: DataFileContent) -> DataFile:
    path = f"{warehouse}/{name}.parquet"
    pq.write_table(rows, path)
    return DataFile.from_args(
        content=content,
        file_path=path,
        file_format=FileFormat.PARQUET,
        partition=Record(value),
        record_count=rows.num_rows,
        file_size_in_bytes=os.path.getsize(path),
    )


class DeleteManifestWriter(ManifestWriterV2):
    def content(self) -> ManifestContent:
        return ManifestContent.DELETES

    @property
    def _meta(self) -> dict[str, str]:  # private: the manifest header names its content
        return {**super()._meta, "content": "deletes"}


# Write files the way Spark or Java would: PyIceberg 0.12 cannot append to a NaN partition, and PyIceberg
# cannot write delete files. Each partition gets two data files and one position delete file that removes
# row 0 of both. A delete file covering two data files has no file_path bounds, so it is partition-scoped.
data_files, delete_files = [], []
for value, ids in [(1.0, [1, 2, 3, 4]), (float("nan"), [5, 6, 7, 8])]:
    for pair in (ids[:2], ids[2:]):
        rows = pa.Table.from_pydict({"id": pair, "value": [value] * 2}, schema=schema.as_arrow())
        data_files.append(write_file(f"data-{pair[0]}", rows, value, DataFileContent.DATA))
    deletes = pa.Table.from_pydict({"file_path": [f.file_path for f in data_files[-2:]], "pos": [0, 0]}, schema=pos_delete_schema)
    delete_files.append(write_file(f"deletes-{ids[0]}", deletes, value, DataFileContent.POSITION_DELETES))

with tbl.transaction() as tx, tx.update_snapshot().fast_append() as append:
    for data_file in data_files:
        append.append_data_file(data_file)

with tbl.transaction() as tx, tx.update_snapshot().overwrite() as overwrite:
    # private: PyIceberg has no delete-manifest writer, so swap one into the snapshot producer
    overwrite.new_manifest_writer = lambda spec: DeleteManifestWriter(
        spec, tbl.schema(), overwrite.new_manifest_output(), overwrite._snapshot_id, "deflate"
    )
    for delete_file in delete_files:
        overwrite.append_data_file(delete_file)

print("expected ids:", [2, 4, 6, 8])
print("actual ids:  ", sorted(tbl.scan().to_arrow()["id"].to_pylist()))
```

Output on main and 0.12.0:

```text
Record(nan) == Record(nan): False; hashes equal: True
expected ids: [2, 4, 6, 8]
actual ids:   [2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
```

The `1.0` partition is correct in every tested version. Version 0.10.0 returns the correct rows in both partitions, even though `Record` equality already fails for NaN there. I also checked per-file position deletes with equal `file_path` bounds separately on main. They work in both partitions, but that control is not included in this script.

[`DeleteFileIndex`](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/blob/e3564a54c10960307147377c578680276865ed18/pyiceberg/table/delete_file_index.py#L115-L137) looks up partition-scoped deletes by `(spec_id, Record)`. [`Record.__eq__`](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/blob/e3564a54c10960307147377c578680276865ed18/pyiceberg/typedef.py#L198-L200) compares lists, so separately decoded NaN partition values compare unequal even though their hashes match. A narrow fix would compare NaN partition values as equal, as Java does through [`StructLikeWrapper`](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/5a2ccf5ba830838ecf182bccb516d5ee48f8b8ed/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/util/StructLikeWrapper.java#L74-L104) and the [float and double comparators](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/5a2ccf5ba830838ecf182bccb516d5ee48f8b8ed/api/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/types/Comparators.java#L35-L41).

The same partition lookup also misses in commit validation, in `_validate_data_files_exist` and `_validate_no_new_deletes_for_data_files`. With the fix for https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/issues/4277 applied, one writer can replace a data file with a copy while another writer adds a partition-scoped delete for a row in it. The replacement commits and brings the deleted row back for good.

Today, main fails earlier with `ValueError: Cannot create expression literal from NaN`, before reaching those checks. A separate required-files check still rejects replacement of a concurrently removed data file.

Java's [default delete granularity is partition](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/5a2ccf5ba830838ecf182bccb516d5ee48f8b8ed/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/TableProperties.java#L429-L430). [`PositionDeleteWriter.metrics()`](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/5a2ccf5ba830838ecf182bccb516d5ee48f8b8ed/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/deletes/PositionDeleteWriter.java#L124-L131) removes the path bounds when a delete file covers multiple data files. Spark writes this shape by default with Iceberg releases before 1.8.0 and with the Spark 3.4 and earlier runtimes. Spark 3.5 and later switched to file granularity in [Iceberg 1.8.0](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/commit/c0d6d42a55a7d33d7d38f73d00e46e86b57d934e). Any Spark version writes it with `write.delete.granularity=partition`.

Related:

- https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/pull/2918 introduced the partition-keyed index, first released in 0.11.0.
- https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/pull/3285 is open and would key equality deletes by the same partition `Record`.
- https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/issues/4277 blocks NaN-partition rewrites on main, so its fix needs to account for the validation failure described here.

I have not run Spark or Java, or tested 0.11.x directly. Java's NaN comparison is based on source inspection.

### Willingness to contribute

- [ ] I can contribute a fix for this bug independently
- [x] I would be willing to contribute a fix for this bug with guidance from the Iceberg community
- [ ] I cannot contribute a fix for this bug at this time

problem_statement.title: [BUG] OpenAPI schema generates invalid `examples` format for query parameters, breaking Swagger UI
problem_statement.body:
**Describe the bug**

When using Pydantic's `examples` field on query parameters, Django Ninja copies the JSON Schema array format directly to the OpenAPI Parameter Object level. However, OpenAPI 3.1.0 requires `examples` at the Parameter Object level to be a map of Example Objects, not an array. This causes Swagger UI to fail with `TypeError: i.get is not a function` when rendering the parameters.

**Reproduction**

```python
from ninja import NinjaAPI, Query, FilterSchema, Field

api = NinjaAPI()


class MyFilters(FilterSchema):
    status: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description="Filter by status",
        examples=["active", "pending", "archived"],
    )


@api.get("/items")
def list_items(request, filters: Query[MyFilters]):
    return {"status": filters.status}


# Check the generated OpenAPI schema
schema = api.get_openapi_schema()
param = schema["paths"]["/api/items"]["get"]["parameters"][0]
print(param)
```

Actual Output

```json
{
  "in": "query",
  "name": "status",
  "schema": {
    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
    "examples": ["active", "pending", "archived"],
    "title": "Status"
  },
  "required": false,
  "examples": ["active", "pending", "archived"]
}
```

The `examples` at the parameter level is an array, which is invalid per OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec.

Expected Output

```json
{
  "in": "query",
  "name": "status",
  "schema": {
    "anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}],
    "examples": ["active", "pending", "archived"],
    "title": "Status"
  },
  "required": false,
  "examples": {
    "example0": {"value": "active"},
    "example1": {"value": "pending"},
    "example2": {"value": "archived"}
  }
}
```

The `examples` inside schema can remain an array (valid JSON Schema), but at the Parameter Object level it must be a map of Example Objects.

**Root Cause**

In [`ninja/openapi/schema.py`](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/d5d977636652e6a024f861ca43c5c91617eaeca0/ninja/openapi/schema.py#L192-L193), the `_extract_parameters` method copies examples directly without format conversion:

```python
if "examples" in p_schema:
    param["examples"] = p_schema["examples"]
```

**Suggested Fix**

Convert the array format to the OpenAPI map format when copying to the parameter level:

```python
if "examples" in p_schema:
    examples = p_schema["examples"]
    param["examples"] = (
        {f"example{i}": {"value": v} for i, v in enumerate(examples)}
        if isinstance(examples, list)
        else examples
    )
```

**References**

- <https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0#parameter-object> - `examples` must be `Map[string, Example Object | Reference Object]`
- <https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/annotations#examples> - array format is valid here

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.13.11
 - Django version: 5.2.9
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.5.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.12.5

problem_statement.title: A blank wake phrase makes WakeCheckFilter pass every transcription
problem_statement.body:
A blank wake phrase turns the wake gate into an open gate, and `compile_phrase_pattern()`'s handling of it is pinned by a test, so I am asking before changing anything.

`compile_phrase_pattern("")` builds `\b\b`, which matches at every word boundary:

```python
from pipecat.utils.string import compile_phrase_pattern

pattern = compile_phrase_pattern("")
print(pattern.pattern)                      # '\\b\\b'
print(len(pattern.findall("anything here")))  # 4 zero-length matches
```

`tests/test_compile_phrase_pattern.py::test_empty_phrase_keeps_previous_behavior` pins exactly that (`assertEqual(compile_phrase_pattern("").pattern, r"\b\b")`), so this looks deliberate rather than accidental.

The consequence shows up one layer up. `WakeCheckFilter` compiles one pattern per entry of the `wake_phrases` list and treats "any pattern matches" as awake, so a blank entry makes every transcription pass:

```python
from pipecat.frames.frames import TranscriptionFrame
from pipecat.processors.filters.wake_check_filter import WakeCheckFilter

# same subclass-of-filter harness as below; counting what reaches the downstream side
filter = WakeCheckFilter(wake_phrases=[""])       # e.g. an unset env var: os.getenv("WAKE", "").split(",")
# then feed "just a normal sentence", "another one", ""
```

Observed, counting transcriptions that the filter pushes downstream:

```text
wake_phrases=["hey pipecat"] -> pushed 0/3   (none contain the phrase: expected)
wake_phrases=[""]            -> pushed 3/3   (every one passes: the gate never gates)
```

`WakePhraseUserTurnStartStrategy` has the same shape: it strips punctuation from each phrase before compiling, so a phrase like `"!!!"` becomes `""` and matches everything as well.

A blank phrase is easy to produce from configuration — `os.getenv("WAKE_PHRASES", "").split(",")` yields `[""]` when the variable is unset, and a spreadsheet or config file with an empty entry does the same. For a wake gate that decides whether the user is addressing the bot, failing open is the wrong direction: the filter ports on every transcript, including other participants'.

Which fix would you prefer?

1. **Reject a blank phrase** in `compile_phrase_pattern()` with a `ValueError`, so both call sites fail at construction with a message that names the problem. This removes the pinned behaviour above, which is why I have not opened a PR.
2. **Skip blank entries at the call sites** (`WakeCheckFilter`, `WakePhraseUserTurnStartStrategy`), leaving `compile_phrase_pattern()` exactly as it is and making a blank entry mean "no wake phrase" rather than "match everything" — the gate then fails closed.

Option 2 keeps the pinned contract and fixes the user-visible behaviour; option 1 is louder at the point of configuration. Happy to send either, with tests, once you say which — or to leave it if the blank-phrase match-all is wanted.

Environment: `main` at `3dbb0c84`, Python 3.13, Windows 11, the repository's venv, no provider keys or network needed.

+    base_snapshot_id = tbl.metadata.current_snapshot_id
+    assert base_snapshot_id is not None
+    tbl.manage_snapshots().create_branch(snapshot_id=base_snapshot_id, branch_name="b").commit()
+
+    tx = tbl.transaction()
+    tx.append(pa.table({"x": [2]}), branch="b")
+    tx.append(pa.table({"x": [3]}))
+    # A second write to main asserts the snapshot staged above; only the base assertion must be kept.
+    tx.append(pa.table({"x": [4]}))
+
+    ref_assertions = {r.ref: r.snapshot_id for r in tx._requirements if isinstance(r, AssertRefSnapshotId)}
+    assert ref_assertions == {"b": base_snapshot_id, "main": base_snapshot_id}
+    assert len([r for r in tx._requirements if isinstance(r, AssertRefSnapshotId)]) == 2

problem_statement.title: A transaction writing two branches overwrites concurrent changes to the second
problem_statement.body:
### Apache Iceberg version

0.12.0 (latest release)

### Please describe the bug 🐞

Currently, `Transaction._stage` drops a requirement whose type is already staged, so a transaction writing two branches sends `AssertRefSnapshotId` for the first only, and a concurrent change to the second is overwritten. With `main` written first, a concurrent rollback of `main` is caught and retried.

```python
import tempfile
import pyarrow as pa
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

cat = SqlCatalog("c", uri="sqlite:///:memory:", warehouse=f"file://{tempfile.mkdtemp()}")
cat.create_namespace("ns")
row = lambda x: pa.table({"x": [x]})
t = cat.create_table("ns.t", schema=row(1).schema)
t.append(row(1))
s1 = t.current_snapshot().snapshot_id
t.append(row(2))
t.manage_snapshots().create_branch(t.current_snapshot().snapshot_id, "b").commit()

cat.load_table("ns.t").manage_snapshots().rollback_to_snapshot(s1).commit()
with t.transaction() as tx:
    tx.append(row(3), branch="b")
    tx.append(row(3))
print(sorted(cat.load_table("ns.t").scan().to_arrow()["x"].to_pylist()))
# [1, 2, 3], should be [1, 3]
# another writer rolled main back to [1] after t was loaded, and this commit put 2 back
```

On a format-version 1 table, another writer's append to `main` is lost the same way.

tested on pyiceberg 0.12.0 and main

### Willingness to contribute

- [ ] I can contribute a fix for this bug independently
- [ ] I would be willing to contribute a fix for this bug with guidance from the Iceberg community
- [ ] I cannot contribute a fix for this bug at this time

problem_statement.title: OpenAILiveLLMService: long Chinese/Japanese context appends are chunked mid-sentence (_chunk_text ignores 。！？)
problem_statement.body:
### pipecat version

`main` (1.14.1.dev)

### Description

`OpenAILiveLLMService._send_context_append()` splits long delegation output into `session.commentary.append` / `session.thinking.append` chunks with `_chunk_text()`, which is meant to break on sentence boundaries. The boundary regex is `(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+`, so it only recognises ASCII punctuation followed by whitespace. Chinese and Japanese end sentences with `。！？` and write no space after them, so a CJK result is treated as one giant "sentence" and `_split_at_token_limit()` cuts it wherever the token budget runs out — in the middle of a sentence (there is no space to fall back to either). The live model then receives half-sentences as separate appends.

### Reproduction

```python
from pipecat.services.openai.live import llm as live_llm

text = "".join(["天気はどうですか。", "今日は晴れです！", "明日は雨ですか？", "这是一个测试句子。"] * 50)
chunks = live_llm._chunk_text(text, 100)
print([c[-3:] for c in chunks])
# ['测试句', '一个测', '这是一', 'か？这', ...]  -> chunks end mid-sentence
```

Mixed text shows the same: `_chunk_text("First sentence. 第二句话。Third sentence.", 6)` returns `['First sentence.', '第二句话。Thir', 'd sentence.']`.

### Expected

Full-width `。！？` should count as sentence boundaries (with no space required after them), so chunks end at the end of a sentence, and CJK sentences are rejoined without inserting spaces.

I have a fix with tests and will open a PR.

problem_statement.title: `POST /flow_runs/{id}/resume` returns 500 when `run_input` contains an integer outside the 64-bit range
problem_statement.body:
### Bug summary

Resuming a paused flow run returns 500 when `run_input` contains an integer outside the 64-bit range. The run stays `PAUSED` and no input is stored. #23429 fixes the same error in the flow run list endpoints, but doesn't change this one.

```python
import sys
import uuid

import httpx

api = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:4200/api"
c = httpx.Client(base_url=api, limits=httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=0))
flow_id = c.post("/flows/", json={"name": f"repro-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"}).json()["id"]
keyset = {"description": "d", "response": "resp", "schema": "sch"}

for value in ["1", str(2**64)]:
    run_id = c.post("/flow_runs/", json={"flow_id": flow_id}).json()["id"]
    c.post(f"/flow_runs/{run_id}/set_state", json={"state": {"type": "RUNNING"}, "force": True})
    c.post(
        f"/flow_runs/{run_id}/set_state",
        json={
            "state": {"type": "PAUSED", "state_details": {"pause_key": "p", "run_input_keyset": keyset}},
            "force": True,
        },
    )
    c.post(f"/flow_runs/{run_id}/input", json={"key": "sch", "value": '{"type": "object"}'})
    r = c.post(
        f"/flow_runs/{run_id}/resume",
        content=b'{"run_input": {"x": %s}}' % value.encode(),
        headers={"content-type": "application/json"},
    )
    state = c.get(f"/flow_runs/{run_id}").json()["state"]["type"]
    print(f"run_input x={value}: resume -> {r.status_code}; state after: {state}")
```

Output:

```
run_input x=1: resume -> 201; state after: RUNNING
run_input x=18446744073709551616: resume -> 500; state after: PAUSED
```

Server error:

```
  File "prefect/server/api/flow_runs.py", line 569, in resume_flow_run
    value=orjson.dumps(run_input).decode("utf-8"),
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: Integer exceeds 64-bit range
```

Expected: the run resumes and the input is stored, or the request gets a 422.

### Version info

```Text
Version:              3.8.6
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.12.13
Git commit:           33de4078
Built:                Mon, Sep 14, 2026 02:21 PM
OS/Arch:              linux/x86_64
Profile:              ephemeral
Server type:          server
Pydantic version:     2.13.4
Server:
  Database:           sqlite
  SQLite version:     3.53.1
```

`main` has the same `orjson.dumps(run_input)` call (`src/prefect/server/api/flow_runs.py:568`).

### Additional context

Related: #15031, #23429.

problem_statement.title: `primary_energy` GlobalConstraint with `investment_period` raises `KeyError` for per-period storage with emissions
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted by AI.

### Version Checks (indicate both or one)

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest [release](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/releases) of PyPSA (1.4.0).
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the current [`master`](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/tree/master) branch of PyPSA (45b56634).

### Issue Description

A `primary_energy` GlobalConstraint that sets `investment_period` raises `KeyError` when a StorageUnit with `state_of_charge_initial_per_period = True`, or a Store with `e_initial_per_period = True`, has a carrier with emissions.

`define_primary_energy_limit` cuts the state of charge to the stated period's snapshots, `period_sns` (`optimization/global_constraints.py:371`). It then selects `period_last_sns`, the last snapshot of every period in the horizon (`:469` for StorageUnit, `:521` for Store). Those snapshots of the other periods are not in `period_sns`, so the selection fails.

The same network without `investment_period` on the constraint solves. Each period's closing level should enter the row only for the period the constraint states.

### Reproducible Example

Run with `uv run --script mre.py`.

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = ["pypsa==1.4.0", "highspy"]
# ///
import pandas as pd

import pypsa

n = pypsa.Network()
n.set_snapshots(pd.MultiIndex.from_product([[2030, 2040], [0, 1]]))
n.investment_periods = [2030, 2040]
n.add("Carrier", "gas", co2_emissions=0.2)
n.add("Bus", "b")
n.add("Load", "d", bus="b", p_set=10)
n.add("Generator", "g", bus="b", p_nom=100, marginal_cost=1, carrier="gas")
n.add(
    "StorageUnit",
    "s",
    bus="b",
    p_nom=10,
    max_hours=2,
    carrier="gas",
    state_of_charge_initial=10,
    state_of_charge_initial_per_period=True,
)
n.add(
    "GlobalConstraint",
    "co2",
    type="primary_energy",
    carrier_attribute="co2_emissions",
    sense="<=",
    constant=1e6,
    investment_period=2030,
)
n.optimize(multi_investment_periods=True)
```

```
  File ".../pypsa/optimization/global_constraints.py", line 469, in define_primary_energy_limit
    soc_final = soc.loc[period_last_sns, sus_per_period.index]
...
KeyError: "not all values found in index 'snapshot'"
```

A Store with `e_initial=10, e_initial_per_period=True` in place of the StorageUnit raises the same error at line 521.

### Expected Behavior

The model builds. For the stated period, the row counts the emissions of the change in level from `state_of_charge_initial` (or `e_initial`) to the level at the last snapshot of that period, weighted by that period's years, as for a constraint without `investment_period`. The other periods' closing levels do not enter the row.

### Installed Versions

<details>

`pypsa==1.4.0`, `linopy==0.10.1`, `xarray==2026.9.0`, `pandas==3.1.0`, `numpy==2.5.4`, `highspy`, Python 3.13. The same output on `master` at 45b566348c9a088dc5dd15ca02ad42ea32de6156.

</details>

problem_statement.title: [Bug] 桌面端 HTML 预览「在浏览器中打开」失效：中文路径弹「找不到文件」，工作区外文件点击无反应
problem_statement.body:
## 环境

- QwenPaw Desktop **v2.3.0b1**（Windows 11 x64，系统区域中文，默认浏览器 Edge）
- 后端：`qwenpaw.exe --version` → `QwenPaw, version 2.3.0b1`
- 工作区路径包含中文目录（下文记作 `<workspace>`）
- 场景：Agent 生成一个依赖 JS 渲染的单文件 HTML（日报仪表盘），在右侧文件预览面板点「在浏览器中打开」

## 复现步骤 A（文件在工作区内，路径含中文）

1. 在工作区 `<workspace>\digest\us\report.html` 生成任意 HTML
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：弹出 Windows 对话框

```
file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/digest/us/report.html
Windows 找不到文件
```

（URL 里的中文目录被 UTF-8 百分号编码）

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 复现步骤 B（文件在纯 ASCII 路径下）

1. 把同一个文件复制到 `<ascii-dir>\report.html`（全 ASCII，无空格）
2. 在预览面板点击「在浏览器中打开」

**实际结果**：**无任何反应**——不弹错误框、不新开窗口、不出新标签页，前台窗口仍是 QwenPaw，浏览器窗口标题未变。

**期望结果**：默认浏览器打开该文件。

## 系统层对照实验（排除文件损坏与关联问题）

在同一台机器上用 `ShellExecuteW`（shell32）分别打开三种形式：

| 传入形式 | 返回值 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 原生路径 `<ascii-dir>\report.html` | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/<ascii-dir>/report.html`（纯 ASCII URL） | 42 | **成功打开** |
| `file:///E:/%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA/.../report.html`（UTF-8 百分号编码） | 2 | 失败（`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`） |

即：**文件本身可打开、系统关联正常、ASCII 的 `file:///` URL 也能打开**，问题出在应用传入的形式上。

## 分析（供参考）

1. **中文路径失败的机制**：Windows 对 `file:///` URL 的百分号解码使用当前 ANSI 代码页（中文系统为 GBK/936），而应用传的是 UTF-8 编码。`%E5%B7%A5%E4%BD%9C%E5%8C%BA` 被按 GBK 解码成乱码，路径不存在 → `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`。
   **建议**：调用 `ShellExecute` 时 `lpFile` 直接传**本地路径**（不要先转成 `file:///` URL 再百分号编码），或对含非 ASCII 字符的路径走 `os.startfile(path)` / `explorer.exe` 原生路径分支。

2. **工作区外文件点击无反应**：疑似 handler 以 `root`（工作区目录）为基准解析 `filePath`，文件在工作区外时解析失败并**静默 return**。
   **建议**：解析失败时至少给出 toast/错误提示；或对绝对路径直接放行。

3. **预览面板的认知成本**：预览不执行 JS，含动态内容的页面只显示模板骨架（本用例里显示的是模板默认标题与空容器），用户容易误判为「文件坏了」。建议动态内容场景下把「在浏览器中打开」做成明确可用的主操作，或提供「以独立窗口打开」。

4. **附带问题（可选）**：该窗口通过 UI Automation 枚举到 **0 个按钮/控件**（疑似 Qt WebEngine 未挂 UIA 桥），导致自动化测试与读屏软件都无法操作该界面。

## 影响

- 任何工作区路径含中文的 Windows 用户（国内用户大概率如此）都无法使用「在浏览器中打开」
- 生成的报告/看板类 HTML（依赖 JS 渲染）在应用内完全无法查看，只能由用户自己去资源管理器双击

*附：问题为使用过程中实测；系统层对照实验在同一台机器上可复现。*

problem_statement.title: compute_flops_per_token fails on MoE configs without num_local_experts (Qwen3.5 MoE, Beam)
problem_statement.body:
### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoConfig
from trl.trainer.utils import compute_flops_per_token

config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained("trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration-3.6")
compute_flops_per_token(config.get_text_config(), seq_len=128)
```

outputs:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 5, in <module>
    compute_flops_per_token(config.get_text_config(), seq_len=128)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/trl/trainer/utils.py", line 1821, in compute_flops_per_token
    num_experts = config.num_local_experts
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/transformers/configuration_utils.py", line 658, in __getattribute__
    return super().__getattribute__(key)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/transformers/integrations/heterogeneity/configuration_utils.py", line 312, in __getattribute__
    return super().__getattribute__(key)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^
AttributeError: 'Qwen3_5MoeTextConfig' object has no attribute 'num_local_experts'
```

On transformers >= 5.1, `compute_flops_per_token` reads the expert count from `num_local_experts`. The Qwen3.5 MoE and Beam configs only have `num_experts`, and neither has `decoder_sparse_step`, which is read next.

### How did you hit this?

Porting GRPO's tests to AsyncGRPO (#8146). `AsyncGRPOTrainer` and `AsyncDistillationTrainer` call `compute_flops_per_token` at every step to log `perf/mfu_*`, so training a Qwen3.5 or Qwen3.6 MoE model, or Beam, raises at the first step. `test_train[tiny-BeamForCausalLM]` and `test_train_vlm_text_only_data[tiny-Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration-3.6]` are expected failures there because of it.

- Python version: 3.13.13
- TRL version: 1.10.0.dev0 (main at bb68a61d5)

problem_statement.title: with evaluate(False): And(Eq(0, Add(x, Mul(-1, I)))) gets RecursionError exception
problem_statement.body:
Running sympy 1.14 in python 3.12 on ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS under WSL 2 on Windows 11, if I run this:

```
from sympy import *
x=symbols("x")
with evaluate(False):
    And(Eq(0, Add(x, Mul(-1, I))))
```

I get this exception:

`RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded`

I get the same error running just the with evaluate part on live.sympy.org. The stack trace is too long to include in this issue text, but it's pretty easy to reproduce.

I made a small attempt to debug this and found that if I run this under the pycharm debugger and do the following it actually runs to completion without the exception.

- Set Variables Loading Policy (in the three-dots menu in the debugger pane toolbar) to Synchronously
- Every time you change that setting you have to restart the interactive python console and reattach the debugger
- Set a breakpoint on the final line of `Expr.__complex__` (line 380 of `core/expr.py`)
- Run the lines above
- Hit step into, step out, step into to get inside the float(im) call
- Hit resume program as many times as necessary (**don't** just remove the breakpoint: that doesn't work)

However, if Variables Loading Policy is instead set to either Synchronously or On-demand and you perform the same steps, you still get the exception.

There are other sequences of stepping/breaking you can do in the debugger (without changing the code or variables) to get the code to run without exception, but this has been the most reliable so far as it sometimes seems that the behavior changes.

problem_statement.title: bug(sdk): enable_caching override does not propagate to tasks in nested DAGs
problem_statement.body:
### Environment

* KFP version: not needed; this is visible in the request the SDK client builds, no cluster required.
* KFP SDK version: `master` at 3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8.
* All dependencies version: `uv sync --frozen --extra dev` on that commit.

### Summary

`Client.run_pipeline(..., enable_caching=False)` (and the other submission methods) is documented to override caching for **all tasks in the pipeline**, but it only rewrites the tasks that sit directly in the root DAG. Tasks inside `dsl.If`, `dsl.ParallelFor`, `dsl.ExitHandler` and nested pipelines keep their compile-time setting in the PipelineSpec that is sent to the API server. The same gap affects `enable_caching=True`: a task compiled with `set_caching_options(False)` inside a nested DAG stays disabled.

### Root cause

[`_override_caching_options`](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/sdk/python/kfp/client/client.py#L2054-L2069) only iterates `pipeline_spec.root.dag.tasks`:

```python
for _, task_spec in pipeline_spec.root.dag.tasks.items():
    task_spec.caching_options.enable_cache = enable_caching
```

The compiler does not put tasks under `dsl.If`, `ParallelFor`, `ExitHandler` or a nested pipeline in the root DAG. Each of those constructs becomes its own DAG component in `pipeline_spec.components` (`comp-condition-N`, `comp-for-loop-N`, `comp-exit-handler-N`, `comp-<pipeline>`), and the tasks live in that component's `dag.tasks`. The root DAG only holds the task that references the sub-DAG, so the loop never reaches the tasks inside it.

Every public submission path goes through this function via [`_create_job_config`](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/sdk/python/kfp/client/client.py#L1162-L1170): `run_pipeline`, `create_recurring_run`, `create_run_from_pipeline_package` and `create_run_from_pipeline_func`.

### Documented contract

`run_pipeline`, `create_recurring_run`, `create_run_from_pipeline_package` and `create_run_from_pipeline_func` all document `enable_caching` the same way ([example](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/sdk/python/kfp/client/client.py#L864-L868)):

> If set, the setting applies to all tasks in the pipeline (overrides the compile time settings).

### How the backend uses the nested task spec

The driver reads caching options per executable task from the PipelineSpec stored on the run, so the stale value in a nested DAG is the one that is used:

1. The driver loads the run's spec with `FetchPipelineSpecFromRun` ([spec_resolution.go#L54](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/driver/driverinputs/spec_resolution.go#L54)).
2. `ScopePath.Push` resolves a nested task's `PipelineTaskSpec` from its parent DAG component, `Components[parent].Dag.Tasks[name]` ([scope_path.go#L197-L208](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/common/util/scope_path.go#L197-L208)). That is the entry the client override skipped.
3. `getFingerPrintsAndID` only skips the cache lookup when `opts.Task.GetCachingOptions().GetEnableCache()` is false (or caching is disabled server-wide) ([cache.go#L108](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/v2/driver/cache.go#L108)). Cached outputs are then reused in [container.go#L356](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/v2/driver/container.go#L356), and in [k8s.go#L1278](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/v2/driver/k8s.go#L1278) / [#L1463](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/3f66a20e42b0e47149cc5520946dfc6a3a7c28b8/backend/src/v2/driver/k8s.go#L1463) for PVC tasks.

The DAG driver does not read caching options, so only executable tasks are affected.

### Steps to reproduce

The script captures the request instead of sending it, so it needs no cluster:

```python
from unittest import mock

from kfp import compiler, dsl
from kfp.client import Client


@dsl.component
def echo(msg: str) -> str:
    return msg


@dsl.pipeline
def inner():
    echo(msg='inner')


@dsl.pipeline
def repro(flag: str = 'yes'):
    exit_task = echo(msg='exit')
    with dsl.ExitHandler(exit_task):
        echo(msg='root')
        with dsl.If(flag == 'yes'):
            echo(msg='if')
            with dsl.ParallelFor(['a', 'b']) as item:
                echo(msg=item)
        inner()


compiler.Compiler().compile(repro, 'repro.yaml')

client = Client.__new__(Client)  # skip cluster discovery; only the request matters
client._run_api = mock.MagicMock()
client._get_url_prefix = lambda: ''
client.run_pipeline(
    experiment_id='e', job_name='j',
    pipeline_package_path='repro.yaml', enable_caching=False,
)
spec = client._run_api.run_service_create_run.call_args.kwargs['run'].pipeline_spec

dags = {'root': spec['root'], **{k: v for k, v in spec['components'].items() if 'dag' in v}}
for dag_name, comp in dags.items():
    for task_name, task in comp['dag']['tasks'].items():
        if 'dag' not in spec['components'][task['componentRef']['name']]:
            print(f'{dag_name:22} {task_name:8} {task.get("cachingOptions")}')
```

Output on `master` (executable tasks only; `{}` is an explicit `false`, which protobuf JSON omits):

```text
root                   echo     {}
comp-for-loop-4        echo-4   {'enableCache': True}
comp-condition-2       echo-3   {'enableCache': True}
comp-exit-handler-1    echo-2   {'enableCache': True}
comp-inner             echo     {'enableCache': True}
```

Only the exit task, which the compiler places in the root DAG, is overridden. The guarded task, the `dsl.If` task, the `ParallelFor` body and the nested pipeline's task are still `enableCache: true`.

### Expected result

Every task in every DAG reachable from the root has `cachingOptions.enableCache` equal to the requested `enable_caching`. When `enable_caching` is not set, the compiled settings are left unchanged.

### Evidence

I have a fix and regression tests ready on [Karman580:fix/nested-dag-caching-override](https://github.com/Karman580/pipelines/tree/fix/nested-dag-caching-override). The tests compile a pipeline with a root task, `dsl.If`, `ParallelFor`, an `ExitHandler` (guarded and exit task) and nested pipelines two levels deep. They pass it through `_create_job_config` and check `caching_options` on every task in the submitted PipelineSpec for `enable_caching=True`, `False` and `None`. A second test checks the traversal on a hand-built spec with a DAG component shared by two tasks, a dangling reference and an unreachable component.

```bash
uv run pytest sdk/python/kfp/client/client_test.py -k "nested_dags or shared_dag"
```

With `client.py` at `master` (3f66a20e4):

```text
E               AssertionError: True != False : comp-exit-handler-1/middle
E       AssertionError: True is not false
E               AssertionError: False is not true : comp-exit-handler-1/condition-2
FAILED sdk/python/kfp/client/client_test.py::TestOverrideCachingOptions::test_submitted_spec_overrides_tasks_in_nested_dags1
FAILED sdk/python/kfp/client/client_test.py::TestOverrideCachingOptions::test_override_visits_shared_dag_once_and_ignores_unreachable
FAILED sdk/python/kfp/client/client_test.py::TestOverrideCachingOptions::test_submitted_spec_overrides_tasks_in_nested_dags0
================= 3 failed, 1 passed, 143 deselected in 0.41s ==================
```

(The `enable_caching=None` case passes on `master` too; it is there to guard against regressions.)

With the fix:

```text
...test_submitted_spec_overrides_tasks_in_nested_dags1 PASSED [ 25%]
...test_override_visits_shared_dag_once_and_ignores_unreachable PASSED [ 50%]
...test_submitted_spec_overrides_tasks_in_nested_dags0 PASSED [ 75%]
...test_submitted_spec_overrides_tasks_in_nested_dags2 PASSED [100%]
====================== 4 passed, 143 deselected in 0.27s =======================
```

`uv run pytest -q sdk/python/kfp/client`: 163 passed on `master`, 167 passed with the fix.

**Backend check (unit level).** A temporary Go test, not part of the fix, loaded the PipelineSpec that the client submits with `enable_caching=False`. It resolved each executable task through `util.ScopePathFromStringPathWithNewTask` and called `getFingerPrintsAndID` with a fake API that always returns a cached task. Both runs ended with `ok`, because the probe logs behaviour rather than asserting it; the difference is in the logged columns:

```text
# spec submitted by the master client
root                                          echo    enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1                           echo-2  enableCache=true  FindCachedTask called=true  hit returned=true
root.exit-handler-1.condition-2               echo-3  enableCache=true  FindCachedTask called=true  hit returned=true
root.exit-handler-1.condition-2.for-loop-4    echo-4  enableCache=true  FindCachedTask called=true  hit returned=true
root.exit-handler-1.middle                    echo    enableCache=true  FindCachedTask called=true  hit returned=true
root.exit-handler-1.middle.inner              echo    enableCache=true  FindCachedTask called=true  hit returned=true

# spec submitted by the fixed client
root                                          echo    enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1                           echo-2  enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1.condition-2               echo-3  enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1.condition-2.for-loop-4    echo-4  enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1.middle                    echo    enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
root.exit-handler-1.middle.inner              echo    enableCache=false FindCachedTask called=false hit returned=false
```

### Limitations

- I have not reproduced stale outputs on a running cluster. On a cluster, a nested task also needs a previous successful execution with the same fingerprint in the namespace to get a cache hit, and server-side `CacheEnabled=false` still disables caching everywhere.
- `cache_key` goes through the same root-only loop. Its intended scope for nested tasks is not documented, and applying one key to every nested task would give all `ParallelFor` iterations the same fingerprint. I am not treating it as part of this bug.

### Related

- #14253 (open): `enable_caching`/`cache_key` are dropped entirely when submitting by `pipeline_id`/`version_id`, because the override only runs on the `pipeline_package_path` branch. That is a different path; a fix for it would reuse `_override_caching_options`, so it would also hit this nested-DAG gap.
- #14255 (closed, not merged): the proposed fix for #14253. It reused the same root-only loop.
- #7912 (merged): introduced the submission-time override with the root-only loop.

I could not find an existing issue for the nested-DAG case.

### Labels

/area sdk

Impacted by this bug? Give it a 👍.

problem_statement.title: _sort_if_not_monotonic uses a stable sort; is stability needed?
problem_statement.body:
`_sort_if_not_monotonic` sorts with `kind="stable"` so duplicate values keep a deterministic physical order. On random int64 keys, `Series.sort_values(kind="stable")` takes 0.78 s at 4M rows and 6.47 s at 16M; `kind="quicksort"` takes 0.33 s and 1.53 s. For large right sides the stable sort is a large share of `conditional_join` time (about 6 s of a 7.8 s `keep="any"` join at 16M rows).

The function is called from `_range_join.py`, `_regions.py`, `_single_range_predicate.py` (twice) and `_not_equals_only.py`. Question: which callers rely on tie order, and can the rest use an unstable sort?

Proposed work:

1. Audit each caller: does anything depend on the order of rows with equal keys (`first`, `last`, `all` output order, aggregation order)?
2. Add a parameter (for example `stable: bool = True`) so callers that do not need stability can opt out. Keeping the default stable leaves every untouched caller unchanged.
3. Benchmark and fuzz against brute force after switching each caller.

The Rust `first` and `last` selection is label-based, and join row order is not a documented contract, so many callers may be safe. That is unverified.

Measured with pandas 3.1.0 and NumPy on Apple Silicon, random int64 keys in [0, 10^6).

problem_statement.title: `pyproject.toml` adapter for `uv` writes to the filesystem within the project root, breaks down in read-only situations
problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

To support `uv` (indeed, a feature not yet production ready in the current implementation), the `pyproject.toml` file gets moved away and the contents at its path mutate. After `uv` completes, `pdm` restores the original `pyproject.toml`.

This doesn't work when the filesystem is read-only (in some place). This design also creates some noise in IDEs that watch the filesystem and thing the VCS working copy is undergoing changes.

problem_statement.title: Sub-page parameters typed with `| None` reject values 3.18.0 accepted
problem_statement.body:
### First Check

- [x] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [x] This is not a security issue (those should be reported via the [security advisory](https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/security/advisories/new) instead).
- [x] This is not a Q&A. I am sure something is wrong with NiceGUI or its documentation.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar [issue](https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/issues) and came up empty.

### Example Code

```python
from nicegui import ui

def a(n: int | float | None = None):
    ui.label(repr(n))

def b(n: int | str | None = None):
    ui.label(repr(n))

def c(n: int | None = None):
    ui.label(repr(n))

@ui.page('/')
@ui.page('/{_:path}')
def index():
    ui.sub_pages({'/a': a, '/b': b, '/c': c})

ui.run()
```

### Description

#6452 made `X | None` annotations convert like `Optional[X]` already did. That conversion uses only the first non-`None` member, so values 3.18.0 passed through as strings now fail:

| URL | 3.18.0 | 3.19.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `/a?n=1.5` | `'1.5'` | error |
| `/a?n=1e3` | `'1e3'` | error |
| `/b?n=abc` | `'abc'` | error |
| `/c?n=` | `''` | error |
| `/a?n=2`, `/b?n=7` | `'2'`, `'7'` | `2`, `7` |

"error" means the sub-page shows `500: sub page /a?n=1.5 produced an error` and the log has `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10` from `PageArguments._convert_parameter`. `Optional[int | float]` behaved like this before 3.19 too; #6452 extended it to the `|` spelling.

Plain `@ui.page` parameters with the same annotations go through FastAPI and give `1.5`, `1000.0`, `'abc'` and `'7'`, and a 422 for `?n=` on `int | None`. Should sub-pages convert the same way? Then the first three rows would work again, `/b?n=7` would give `'7'` as on plain pages, and `?n=` on `int | None` would stay an error. Or should an empty value become `None` there?

I have a patch for either direction and can open a PR if that's welcome.

### NiceGUI Version

3.19.0

### Python Version

3.12.11

### Browser

Other

### Operating System

macOS

### Additional Context

Found by comparing v3.18.0 and v3.19.0 with the `User` fixture, so no browser is involved.

+def has_device() -> bool:

problem_statement.title: Runtime advertises cuda_ipc even when it has no usable GPU
problem_statement.body:
A Tesseract served with `gpu_transport="cuda_ipc"` advertises `cuda_ipc` in `x-supported-gpu-transports` even when it can't use a GPU, because `available_gpu_transports()` returns the configured transport without checking it. For example, a server started with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` still offers `cuda_ipc`.

Clients do recover, since `HTTPClient.resolve_gpu_transport` checks a transport before using it. Automatic selection warns and falls back to host copies, and an explicitly requested `cuda_ipc` raises. But the error shows up on the client, at the first call with GPU arrays, rather than where the misconfiguration is.

The server can't detect every failure, because `cuda_ipc` also needs the client to share its host and GPU. It can detect the obvious ones, though: no visible CUDA device, or CUDA failing to initialize. When a device transport is configured, the runtime could check for these at startup and either:

- refuse to start, with an error naming the cause, or
- log a warning and stop advertising the transport.

Refusing to start seems better when the transport was configured explicitly, but either would help.

This came up in review of pasteurlabs/tesseract-torch#73. Its test `test_falls_back_to_host_when_cuda_ipc_does_not_work` produces this state on purpose by hiding the GPU from the server. Seen with tesseract-core 1.15.0.
